correctness.rationale: For the stated normalizations additive-character orthogonality gives q⁻⁴ times the squared triple-fiber sums, and the cited sharp theorem supplies constant modulus for each nonzero optimizer and attainment by constants. At modulus one, equality with the constant saturates each triangle bound, so triple products agree on each fiber. The two translated triples in Step 2 give (T−1)³(T+1)u=0 in R/Z. Its consequence w=(T−1)³u being anti-invariant under T makes it 2-torsion since T has odd order; the telescoping orbit sum gives pw=0, hence w=0. Applying T^p=1 to u and to Δu gives pΔ²u=pΔu=0, reducing the nonconstant phase to F_p. On each affine line it is quadratic; in the induction for A+vB+v²C the fourth coefficient on (x+tw,v+t) is the quadratic part of C at w, then the third coefficient with C's quadratic part zero is C₁(w)+B₂(w); w↦−w separates its odd and even terms. The trace representation and polarization convert the conic identity into independent linearized coefficients. For each j>0 the cleared conic expression has formal θ² coefficient −3, since p^j≥5; its degree and the two omitted parameters total at most 2p^(n−1)+4<q. Thus only the scalar multiplication trace term survives. Translation in frequency proves sufficiency; testing at t=0, separating odd and even parts, then polarizing and using trace nondegeneracy proves distinctness of all q² classes. The bundled exact tests at 5,7,25,49 check fiber ranks, totals and degree-two Frobenius witnesses, not the arbitrary-field theorem; I inspected but did not execute the frozen script.
